title: Analysis of Vitamin A and E in Serum Using HPLC with UV and Fluorescence Detection
author: Geraldine Magnin

steps.title: Protect vitamins from light
steps.instruction: Work with all vitamin solutions and extracts in amber containers or under subdued lighting to avoid photodegradation.

steps.title: Prepare required stock solutions
steps.instruction: Obtain or prepare all standard and internal‑standard solutions needed for the assay.

substeps.instruction: Obtain Vitamin Sock Solution A (a‑tocopherol 160 ppm, retinol 16 ppm in ethanol); concentrations have been confirmed by UV‑spectrophotometry.
Obtain internal‑standard mixture (a‑tocopheryl acetate 20 ppm, retinyl acetate 0.5 ppm in ethanol).
Prepare retinyl acetate 1 000 ppm in acetonitrile: weigh 10 mg retinyl acetate into a 10 mL volumetric flask and fill to volume with acetonitrile.
Prepare calibration working standards of a‑tocopherol and retinol in acetonitrile at the specified ppm levels and store them at –20 °C.

steps.title: Weigh serum sample
steps.instruction: Weigh exactly 1 g of serum into a 15 mL polypropylene tube.

steps.title: Add internal standard and precipitate proteins
steps.instruction: Spike the serum with internal standards and precipitate proteins before extraction.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the internal‑standard spike mix (a‑tocopheryl acetate 20 ppm and retinyl acetate 0.5 ppm in ethanol) and vortex briefly.
Add 2 mL of ethanol containing 0.04 % BHT to the tube.
Add 4 mL of cyclohexane containing 0.04 % BHT and vortex for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Collect cyclohexane layer
steps.instruction: Separate the organic phase and prepare it for evaporation.

substeps.instruction: Using a pipette, remove 2 mL from the top cyclohexane layer and transfer it to a disposable borosilicate glass tube.

steps.title: Evaporate cyclohexane
steps.instruction: Dry the collected cyclohexane under vacuum.

substeps.instruction: Place the glass tube in a Labconco vacuum concentrator set to the minimum temperature (35 °C) and evaporate until dry (≈1 hour for 20 samples).

steps.title: Reconstitute residue
steps.instruction: Redissolve the dried extract in acetonitrile.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.2 mL acetonitrile to the residue, vortex for 20 seconds, and transfer the solution to a 0.5 mL polypropylene microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge extract (high speed)
steps.instruction: Clarify the reconstituted extract before HPLC injection.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the microcentrifuge tube for 10 minutes at 13 000 g and +4 °C.
Transfer 50 µL of the supernatant to an amber HPLC vial equipped with a polypropylene insert.
Store the remaining extract at –20 °C.

steps.title: Optional low‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Perform an additional centrifugation step if required by the workflow.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 3 200 g at room temperature for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Set HPLC injection parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the autosampler and detector settings for vitamin analysis.

substeps.instruction: Set injection volume to 20 µL and program a needle wash with acetonitrile.
For retinol and retinyl acetate, set excitation 325 nm and emission 470 nm.
For a‑tocopherol, set excitation 295 nm and emission 330 nm.

steps.title: Start HPLC system
steps.instruction: Launch the instrument software and prepare the run.

substeps.instruction: Open Empower 3 on the desktop.
Load the method used for the vitamin analysis.
Purge the lines if necessary, start the pump, enable autosampler refrigeration, and turn on the detectors.

steps.title: Load samples and standards
steps.instruction: Place all calibration standards, internal‑standard solution (diluted 2×), and extracted samples into the autosampler tray.

substeps.instruction: Click the “Start” button in Empower 3.

steps.title: Process data in Empower
steps.instruction: Apply calibration and integration settings to obtain quantitative results.

substeps.instruction: Load the Empower 3 method for data processing.
Use external calibration (internal standards are not present in calibration standards); note that calculated concentrations do not include recovery correction.
Integration parameters have been preset from the standards (UV and fluorescence).
Apply linear calibration with a weighting factor of 1/x².

steps.title: Export and calculate results
steps.instruction: Generate a spreadsheet and compute recoveries and concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Export the processed data to an Excel spreadsheet.
Calculate recovery for each sample by comparing the peak area of the internal standards in the sample with that of the internal‑standard mixture.
Calculate the concentrations of retinol, retinyl acetate, and a‑tocopherol in each sample.
